title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles were deployed into a high-congestion event without sufficient battery reserves to handle the actual traffic conditions that materialized. At least a dozen vehicles became immobilized on San Francisco streets after Fourth of July celebrations, requiring roadside assistance towing. The deployment lacked either pre-event planning for predictable peak congestion, or real-time decision-making to route vehicles away from areas where they could strand.

The incident shows a mismatch between the operating conditions a system was designed for and the conditions it encountered in the world. Heavy traffic during major public events is foreseeable in San Francisco, yet the vehicles' battery management did not account for extended idle time in gridlock. It is not established whether Waymo could have predicted this particular traffic pattern, or what specific gaps in traffic modeling or contingency planning allowed vehicles to be positioned where they would run out of power.

One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, and passengers reported vehicles continuing to operate amid active hazards, but the primary incident documented is battery depletion in congestion.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained in heavy traffic. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, mostly Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up after the Golden Gate Bridge fireworks display. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. Waymo's roadside assistance team towed away the vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during heavy traffic events.

The incident prompted complaints from residents stuck in standstill traffic for extended periods. One passenger reported her Waymo began driving despite fireworks being set off on the street, while another person said he spent nearly two hours in gridlock as multiple Waymo vehicles blocked a roadway. A Waymo vehicle also caught fire after driving over fireworks, with no injuries reported. Mayor Daniel Lurie said city officials will meet with stakeholders to prevent similar traffic problems during future events.
